The model assumes normally distributed residuals and independent observations. This formulation allows for empirical estimation of coefficients via least squares minimization. The regression serves as a foundational kernel for GSI’s Bayesian inference pipeline, enabling probabilistic forecasts of team performance. Dualities emerge in how linear models approximate complex non-linear phenomena—such as the interplay between runs scored and allowed—which are captured through additive contributions. Failure modes arise when multicollinearity undermines coefficient stability or when non-linear dependencies are ignored. These limitations inform cross-layer veto conditions ensuring robustness across varying regimes of team performance.
